data.summary: Most machine_overheat alarms are logged as real and carry far more downtime and cost than false alarms, but most incidents lack a same-hour telemetry failure signal, with weather showing only a temperature association.

findings.claim: 74 machine_overheat incidents are logged as real alarms (false_alarm=false) versus 26 logged as false alarms (false_alarm=true).
Real alarms sum 709.9 downtime_min and 1066539 cost_usd, while false alarms sum 32.3 downtime_min and 48559 cost_usd.
95 of 100 overheat incidents have no telemetry failure or heat_dissipation_failure signal in the incident hour, while only 5 have such a signal.
Machine_overheat incidents coincide with higher mean outdoor temperature (24.4C versus 21.3C) and a higher share above 30C (7.0% versus 1.1%) than other incidents.

data.recommendation: Treat machine_overheat alarms as genuine faults and prioritize inspection of affected machines, while auditing the 26 false-alarm entries and 95 no-signal incidents for sensor or calibration issues.
